subject: Zayda Ortiz State Representative Candidacy
overview: State Representative candidate Zayda Ortiz discussed her platform for the 35th Middlesex District, focusing on community-led advocacy and legislative reform. The interview detailed her priorities regarding housing stability, healthcare equity, and infrastructure improvements for Medford and Malden.

items.title: Podcast Introduction
items.summary: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan introduced guest Zayda Ortiz, a candidate for the 35th Middlesex District state representative seat.

items.title: Candidate Background and Activism
items.summary: Ortiz described her transition from healthcare administration to full-time activism, highlighting her role in founding a mutual aid group and advocating for a municipal eviction moratorium.

items.title: Equity, Inclusion, and Healthcare
items.summary: The candidate discussed the necessity of centering racial equity in policy and shared personal experiences of medical bias to emphasize the need for maternal health improvements.

items.title: Housing Crisis and Renter Advocacy
items.summary: Ortiz emphasized her perspective as a renter and advocated for equitable housing solutions that support both homeownership and the ability for seniors to age in place.

items.title: Local Infrastructure and State Funding
items.summary: To address Medford's specific infrastructure needs, the candidate proposed utilizing Fair Share Amendment revenue to fund local road repairs and school construction.

items.title: State House Productivity and Consensus Building
items.summary: Ortiz critiqued the current lack of productivity at the State House and pledged to use her organizing experience to build legislative consensus and move progressive bills forward.

items.title: Transportation and Environmental Policy
items.summary: Policy priorities included restoring eliminated bus routes and increasing investment in public transit to improve environmental resilience.

items.title: Constituent Services and Election Schedule
items.summary: The interview concluded with a commitment to transparent constituent services and a reminder regarding the September 3 primary election.
